problem_framing.rationale: The decision is framed exactly as posed (enter or not, and by which route). All five board constraints (cap, payback, margin floor, ambition, one-launch bandwidth) are listed on the key-questions slide and reused as the test columns in the option comparison. The document identifies early that Option A's cap and floor do not bind and that payback is the real test, hinging on ad cost. Scope exclusions are stated. The only quibble is reading the bandwidth limit as lapsing in 2028, which the pack does not say.

storyline_coherence.rationale: The governing thought answers the question, the five executive-summary points are the five sections, and almost every title is a claim its slide supports; the titles alone give the argument. Three flaws keep it from a 5. The headline low point of $1.9M and the option table use the 25% plan case, which the document itself calls unrealistic; at its own 28% base the figure is $2.4M. The repeat-purchase gate (31% floor, pilot at 29%, 'fix before more SKUs') clashes with the next step of launching four SKUs in Q2 2027. Section-summary slides and five contents slides repeat material.

evidence_and_reasoning.rationale: I re-derived every key figure and found no numerical errors. Unit contribution is $10.725 before ads, $4.725 at 25% ACoS and $7.545 in retail. Option A cumulative cash is 2.40 / 0.38 / -2.32 at 25% / 28% / 32%, with break-even at 28.6% (26.9% at a 25% duty) and 0.08 at 80% volume. Option B reaches -20.8 on plan, -24.3 without the halo and -26.4 at 2.6 units; group margin is 4.46% in 2027. Japan reaches 1.8 with a cross-over at 25.9% ACoS. All critical evidence is used, including evidence against the recommendation (32% benchmark, Japan beating A on cash, two stalled Amazon-first peers). The correlation memo is handled correctly, and claims are mostly calibrated ('pattern, not proof'). Remaining weaknesses are small: growth is given as cumulative rather than CAGR, a few inferences are stated as fact (Japan slot in 2028, Saebom sequencing), and the linear pilot extrapolation ignores slowing monthly gains.

strategic_judgment.rationale: The recommendation is clear and defensible: Amazon-led with numeric gates, retail deferred to 20% awareness (correctly raised from the CEO's 15% using the 3.5 median against the 4.0 line), $40M reset, owners and dates. Alternatives are compared on the board's criteria and the Japan trade-off is stated candidly. It falls short of a 5 on four points. The 28% ceiling sits below the 32% scaling median, so the gate is likely to trip, and the prescribed response (slow the ramp) undermines payback on the document's own 80%-volume sensitivity; this is not reconciled. There is no stop or exit criterion, and the board is not asked to pre-decide whether a payback miss is acceptable. The repeat gate is already unmet at launch. A lower fixed-cost variant to protect payback is not explored, and '$40M after retail' is asserted without economics.

clarity_and_concision.rationale: The answer is on the summary slide in plain, precise language, with quantified titles throughout. But 45 slides, including five contents slides, four section-summary slides that repeat their sections, and eight backups, is longer than this decision needs. The core case could be made in about half the body.

unsupported_claims.quote: the one-launch limit applies only to 2027, so Japan can follow in 2028
unsupported_claims.why: The pack states the bandwidth constraint only for 2027. It does not say management will be free for a second major launch in 2028 while the US is still ramping.

unsupported_claims.quote: Saebom reached about $30M through Amazon, then added 300 doors in 2025
unsupported_claims.why: The pack gives about $30M US revenue in 2025 and doors added in 2025. It does not say the $30M was reached through Amazon alone before the doors.

unsupported_claims.quote: Bigger brands have both more doors and bigger ad budgets
unsupported_claims.why: A plausible confounder, but stated as fact; the pack has no data on ad budgets by brand size.

unsupported_claims.quote: Treat $40M as a post-2030 goal, reached by adding retail once awareness allows
unsupported_claims.why: No numbers show retail closes the gap. The document's own analysis shows retail fixed costs at about seven times shelf contribution.

unsupported_claims.quote: Every month up: no month fell, so June's pace is not yet a ceiling
unsupported_claims.why: Monthly gains slowed from 1,700 to 1,100 units in the last two months. Six rising months do not establish that growth continues, and the 366,000-unit extrapolation leans on this.

logical_contradictions.quote_a: 90-day repeat purchase floor 31%, every quarter by SKU; if met add SKUs as planned; if missed fix labels and range before more SKUs ... Pilot at 29%
logical_contradictions.quote_b: Launch four new SKUs; report blended ad cost and repeat purchase every quarter — US launch lead — From Q2 2027
logical_contradictions.why: The pilot is already below the 31% floor, so the gate's own rule says not to add SKUs yet the plan launches four new SKUs at once.

logical_contradictions.quote_a: Ad cost ceiling (blended ACoS) 28% ... if missed, cut broad-keyword spend and slow the ramp
logical_contradictions.quote_b: At 80% of plan volume, end-2030 cash is only $0.1M even at 25% ad cost
logical_contradictions.why: The remedy for breaching the ad-cost gate (slower ramp, lower volume) itself removes the payback the gate is meant to protect. Not a strict contradiction, but an unreconciled tension in the gating logic.

recommendation.summary: Enter the US in 2027 through an Amazon-led launch with Onsoo's own entity and seven SKUs, under four gates: ACoS at or below 28% (about 27% if the duty rises to 25%), a mid-2027 duty review, a 31% repeat floor, and 20% aided awareness plus $10M on Amazon before any retail. Reject the 600-door retail launch, defer the Japan scale-up to 2028, and reset $40M to a post-2030 goal (about $26M in 2030).
recommendation.rationale: It meets all four defensibility criteria. Options are compared on cap, payback and margin floor. The 25% ACoS and 4.5 units/door assumptions are tested against the benchmarks. The payback condition is stated (ACoS at or below 28.6%, or 26.9% at a 25% duty) with gates and triggers. It says explicitly that no route reaches $40M by 2030 within the constraints. Weaknesses are the lack of an exit criterion and the unreconciled 'slow the ramp' response.

hypothesis_handling.rationale: The document keeps the CEO's Amazon-first route and tightens its terms on a dedicated from-to slide. The 25% plan ACoS is replaced by a 28% ceiling tested against the 32% benchmark, the retail trigger is raised from 15% to 20% awareness using the sell-through bands and the 4.0 delisting line, and the $40M goal is reset to about $26M in 2030. It surfaces the contradictions (plan ACoS vs benchmark, 4.5 vs 2.6 units, ambition vs constraints, Saebom vs the two stalled brands, correlation vs causation) and quantifies ACoS, tariff and volume uncertainty. The one causal overreach is asserting that adding retail later will deliver $40M.

output.overall_comment: Weighted score 4.4 (framing 5, coherence 4, evidence 5, judgment 4, clarity 4). I re-derived every key figure and found no numerical errors: unit economics, Option A cash under the ACoS and tariff cases, the 28.6% and 26.9% break-evens, Option B's -$20.8M and 4.5% margin, the corrected Option B cases, and the Japan cross-over at 25.9% ACoS. Q6 is marked correct although growth is given as cumulative (89% vs 22%) rather than CAGR; the two are equivalent and the 14.7% share matches. The document reaches all nine key insights and avoids all seven traps. The recommendation is the key's preferred answer (R1), with numeric gates and a reset of the $40M ambition. The main weaknesses are in judgment and structure. The 28% ceiling sits below the 32% scaling benchmark, and the stated response (slow the ramp) would itself break payback on the document's own volume sensitivity; there is no explicit exit criterion. The repeat gate is already unmet at launch, yet four SKUs launch anyway. Headline figures use the 25% plan case that the document discredits. Deferring Japan to 2028 and '$40M after retail' are asserted without support. The deck is longer and more repetitive than the decision needs.
